parts.article:
Good morning. Over the last few weeks, we've been talking about the challenges of producing food for the global population. And there's been a lot of interest recently in new sources of food, and one of the most interesting is insects. Well, why should insects be considered as a food source? Well, for a start, a number of them are full of protein, and many also have certain vitamins, which may surprise you more so than a typical farm animal. In fact. And compared to farm animals whose waste products contain a great deal of ammonia, the waste products of insects are far less acidic and would therefore do very little damage to the soil or to any of the rivers that run through farmland. Furthermore, when it comes to the production of insects, the expense would be very low. No trees need be chopped down or forests turn to pasture. So the space that they would occupy would be radically smaller than for, say, cows or sheep.

But even if some consumers decided that they'd rather not put in six in their shopping basket, we could also consider how insects might be added to animal feed, the food given to farm animals. It's already known that some insects, if they were part of the animal feed, would act as a sort of natural antibiotic within a cow or sheep's digestive system, thus removing the need for human intervention. This would be a cost effective and environmentally friendly alternative for farmers.

However, if consumers do decide that insects are a potential superfood, a way of feeding the world, then the next question is, where do we source them from? The wild, perhaps? Or should there be bread on insect farms? Well, if we take from the wild, one potential consequence of this is that too many will be taken and in turn, a species could become endangered or extinct. Then for insects which are harvested from the wild, we have no way of knowing where they have been or what they have come in contact with. And this could have harmful consequences for human health.

Imagine the scenario if food producers or retailers were supplied with insects that were carrying bacteria, this is not something we wanna add to the food chain. If insects are bred on farms, the problems I've just outlined could be avoided. And in many countries, it's already the case that demand for insects is growing, really growing. And it's not in rural areas where you'd expect, but in fact, in the cities in Thailand, for example, where the demand has really shot up. However, people in countries where insects are traditionally what people eat, they'll tell you that when insects are intensively farmed, their taste is simply not the same. Ironically, this is the same accusation that people have when it comes to the way that cows and sheep are raised.

Insect farmers also face a series of challenges, and researchers are keen to assist. First of all, when it comes to breeding, different insects have different requirements. For a start, it's essential to maintain a suitable temperature for many species to reproduce. If this isn't right, nothing's going to happen. Another problem is something that often happens when any species is bred in a confined space. And so far, researchers and farmers have not come up with any clear or long term effective solution to it. We're talking about the problem of disease. You don't want a whole colony wiped out in one go. There's also the question of where insects need to be kept. If insects are to be bred as a superfood, then the tanks used to house them have to be better designed. And this has to happen so that cleaning takes up less time. If we're talking about mass production, we don't want this to be a time consuming activity. And finally, like I said before, insects have long been part of the diet in some countries, but not so in others. If farmers want to encourage people and say England or France or Germany to eat and 6, then they're gonna have to develop a strategy. And I'm not talking about production, but marketing, something that'll persuade potential customers to try something different. Well, I've given you a general overview of the situation. Now let's look at some specific examples.

analyses.content: 录音在提到昆虫富含蛋白质后，紧接着用“also”引出了它们还含有某些维生素（vitamins）。
Well, for a start, a number of them are full of protein, and many also have certain vitamins, which may surprise you more so than a typical farm animal.
注意单词拼写，虽然结尾有 /z/ 的音，但不要漏掉复数形式。
...the waste products of insects are far less acidic and would therefore do very little damage to the soil or to any of the rivers that run through farmland.
你可能会听到“farmland”，但它是题目中已有的信息，你需要填入的是受保护的对象“rivers”。
录音提到昆虫排泄物酸性低，因此对土壤和流经农田的河流（rivers）几乎没有伤害。
So the space that they would occupy would be radically smaller than for, say, cows or sheep.
你可能会被前面的“expense”或者“trees/forests”干扰，但对应“required”这个需求概念的核心词是“space”。
录音通过与牛羊对比，指出昆虫生产所需的空间（space）要小得多。
It's already known that some insects, if they were part of the animal feed, would act as a sort of natural antibiotic within a cow or sheep's digestive system...
这个单词较长，听题时要注意其发音，不要因为纠结拼写而漏掉后面的信息。
录音提到昆虫加入饲料后，在动物消化系统中能起到天然抗生素（antibiotic）的作用。
Imagine the scenario if food producers or retailers were supplied with insects that were carrying bacteria, this is not something we wanna add to the food chain.
你可能会想填“contact”或“health”，但题目问的是昆虫“包含（contain）”的东西，即具体的致病源。
录音警告说野外采集的昆虫可能携带细菌（bacteria），从而对人类健康产生危害。
录音用“not... but...”结构转折，强调需求增长的地方不是在农村，而是在城市（cities）。
And it's not in rural areas where you'd expect, but in fact, in the cities in Thailand, for example, where the demand has really shot up.
你可能会听到“Thailand”就想填国家名，但题目问的是国家里的什么地方（in the...），所以应填入“cities”。
However, people in countries where insects are traditionally what people eat, they'll tell you that when insects are intensively farmed, their taste is simply not the same.
听到“not the same”时，要立刻反应出它对应题目中的“affected（被影响/改变）”，其主语“taste”即为答案。
录音指出，大规模人工养殖的昆虫，其味道（taste）会变得和野生的不一样（即受到影响）。
And so far, researchers and farmers have not come up with any clear or long term effective solution to it. We're talking about the problem of disease.
你可能会在前面的“confined space”纠结，但“deal with”对应的是“solution”，其针对的问题核心是“disease”。
录音提到对于在狭小空间养殖经常出现的问题——疾病（disease），目前还没有有效的解决办法。
...the tanks used to house them have to be better designed. And this has to happen so that cleaning takes up less time.
你可能会想填“designed”，但题目问的是什么动作变快了，对应原文中“takes up less time”的动作主语。
录音说改进坦克箱的设计是为了让清理（cleaning）工作变得更快（less time）。
And I'm not talking about production, but marketing, something that'll persuade potential customers to try something different.
注意“not... but...”结构，排除掉干扰项“production”，锁定转折后的重点词。
录音明确区分了生产和营销，指出为了劝说人们尝试吃昆虫，需要开发营销（marketing）策略。
